data.name: Aliens versus Predator Classic 2000
data.detailed_description:
Aliens Versus Predator Classic 2000 features the Colonial Marine, Alien and Predator Campaigns and the frenetic single-player Skirmish mode from the original title: Alien Versus Predator Gold Edition, which was released to massive acclaim in 2000.
Alien Versus Predator Classic 2000 has been updated to run on modern PCs and laptops using DirectX 9.0c and includes support for Xbox 360 Controller for Windows.
The three most ferocious species in the universe in a bloodthirsty battle for the ultimate prize: survival. Take your pick: be a Colonial Marine, a Predator or an Alien. Fight through suspense-filled environments: from starships and space stations to colonial bases and eerie planetscapes. One wrong move turns you from hunter to prey.
  • Three campaigns: Colonial Marine, Alien and Predator
  • Includes all the levels from the original AvP Gold Edition plus the Millennium Expansion Pack
  • Skirmish mode against infinite Alien hordes
  • Bonus Episodes
  • Unique abilities, weapons and equipment for each species
  • Scale walls and elevator shafts as an ALIEN with frightening speed as you attack and devour your victims
  • Stalk your prey as the deadly PREDATOR using wrist blades, shoulder cannons and stealth mode
  • Lock and load as a COLONIAL MARINE using motion trackers, grenade launchers and flame-throwers to exterminate your foes
  • Supports Xbox 360 Controller for Windows
  • Music from the original soundtrack CD

Multiplayer Features

  • Integrated with Steam Overlay
  • Uses Steam name
  • Host/Join games via bare-bones in-game lobby browser
  • Can invite and join friends and others via the Steam overlay
  • Game attempts host migration
  • Dedicated servers are not supported or planned

reviews.review:
This game kind of traumatized me as a kid when I found out that the human civilians would just stand there sobbing with their head in their hands if you ran up but didn't kill them as the Alien or Predator. They hired some grade-A actors and actresses for the part, too. It still stands as one of the most genuinely disturbing features in any game I've played.

It also asks me to potentially break My Immersion if I want a clear conscience. Am I the one xenomorph with a sense of empathy? Should I only slaughter the Marines? The Predator would grant mercy, canonically, without a doubt, but the xeno? Some of the civilians do have Molotov cocktails, which hurt like the dickens, but after throwing them in terror they just run away and cry pitifully in the corner. Who can blame them? But perhaps my health is low - I can regain a big chunk if I punch-tongue their brain-box.

AvP 2000 acts like it doesn't even know it's posing this dilemma. It's generating emergent moral crises. It's asking me how much of myself I'm willing to lose. It's asking me if an anthropomorphic alien parasite can defy his physiology and not be a dickhead. It poses the hazards of utilitarianism more effectively than BioShock's option to harvest the Little Sisters, and with far more subtlety. What if this was really the point of the game?

AvP has its flaws - characters, including the player, are so lightning fast it's almost a satire of the ridiculous speed of FPS avatars in the 90s. The signposting is non-existent. You can't manually reload any of your weapons. But it questions you, interrogates even. It gets inside you like the lethal embryo your character once was.

AvP is the answer to the question "can videogames really stand up to literature and cinema?"

No. No they can't. But they can make a 14 year-old boy pause, quit the game with a trembling hand, and go lie down with a bad feeling in his tummy.
